name: gpg2john - Crack PGP/GPG Private Key Passphrase
description: Extract the passphrase hash from a PGP/GPG private key file and crack it offline with john. Useful when you find .keys, .gpg, or .asc private key files on a target - the passphrase protects the private key, and cracking it gives you the ability to decrypt PGP-encrypted data (emails, password stores like passpie, encrypted files).
notes:
=== THE IDEA ===
PGP/GPG private keys are encrypted with a passphrase. gpg2john extracts
the passphrase-derived hash so it can be cracked offline with john.

=== EXTRACT HASH ===
  gpg2john <private_key_file> > gpg.hash
  # The key file can be .keys, .gpg, .asc, or raw PGP private key block
  # If the file has BOTH public and private keys, gpg2john handles it

=== CRACK WITH JOHN ===
  john --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt gpg.hash --format=gpg

=== CRACK WITH HASHCAT ===
  # Not directly supported - use john for GPG hashes

=== THEN USE THE KEY ===
  # Import the key into your GPG keyring
  gpg --import <private_key_file>
  # Decrypt a file/message
  gpg --decrypt <encrypted_file>
  # For passpie: export the password store
  passpie export ~/passwords.db  # enter the cracked passphrase

=== WHERE TO FIND PGP KEYS ===
  ~/.gnupg/
  ~/.passpie/.keys
  /home/*/.gpg
  /opt/*/keys/
  Application config directories

examples.label: Extract hash and crack GPG passphrase
Just extract the hash for review

recommended.note: Cracked GPG passphrase unlocks passpie password stores.

defense.why_it_works: PGP private keys are symmetrically encrypted with a passphrase-derived key. gpg2john extracts the encrypted key material into a format john can brute-force. Weak passphrases crack quickly.
defense.prerequisites: Access to a PGP/GPG private key file on the target system.
defense.impact: Decryption of all data encrypted to that PGP key - emails, password stores, encrypted files.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1552.004] File access to .gnupg directories or .keys files (auditd rules); no network indicator since cracking is offline.
defense.artifacts: Access to .gnupg/ or .keys files in filesystem audit logs; cracked passphrase used to decrypt data.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=linux:audit key="access" name="*.keys" OR name="*.gpg" OR name="secring*"
| table _time, user, name, success
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage contains ".gnupg" or SyslogMessage contains ".keys" or SyslogMessage contains "secring"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Use strong passphrases on PGP keys; restrict file permissions on private keys (600); use hardware tokens (YubiKey) for PGP keys; monitor access to .gnupg directories.
